page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs, which map to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include any local NVMe SSD storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% category. Similarly, Geekbench scores for single-core and multi-core operations are in the bottom 10%, reflecting limited computational speed for demanding tasks like software compilation and image processing. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers measured at 24.13 GB/sec and write operations at 20.93 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 25%. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in text generation for small LLM inference using a 135M model at 104.71 tokens/sec, though prompt processing remains weak at 258.44 tokens/sec.

The e2-standard-4 offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio without the premium cost of high-performance compute tiers. The primary tradeoff is its lower processing throughput and lack of local storage, which limits its utility for I/O-intensive databases or high-performance computing. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving with static web serving throughput at 4.19 GB/sec, small-scale background utilities, and development or testing environments that do not require high-frequency CPU execution.
